title: The Morning Commit · Friday, November 27, 2026
lead: SolidCraft: a free, open-source Fusion 360-style CAD app in Rust that runs in your browser, and lets your AI agent do the modeling
deck: Sketch, constrain, extrude, fillet, and change one dimension to watch the whole part rebuild. SolidCraft runs as a desktop app, in a browser tab, as a CLI, and as an MCP server so Claude Code or other agents can design parts with you. Wes Bos called it a “clean room” port of Fusion 360 and is already printing gears from it.

title: The Morning Commit · Thursday, November 26, 2026
lead: Karpathy had Claude turn real US data into a Civilization-style map you can browse in your browser. Open it and play
deck: Andrej Karpathy asked Claude to populate a Civ-style game map with real public data: Census, BLS, NOAA, USGS, FAA and more, reconciled onto a 25 km hex grid with 19 lenses and a City View for 524 metros. Seven hours and 45K lines of code later, it's live at karpathy.ai/usaciv.

title: The Morning Commit · Wednesday, November 25, 2026
lead: trynix.dev boots real Linux apps in a browser tab, even Firefox running inside Firefox. Open it and play
deck: A Linux kernel compiled to WebAssembly now powers trynix.dev: pick almost any program Nix has ever packaged, and it boots in your browser with windows, OpenGL, sound and networking. No server runs your code; it all happens in the tab.

title: The Morning Commit · Tuesday, November 24, 2026
lead: Ladybird, the browser with a brand-new engine written from scratch, is out in alpha. Download it and try your favourite sites
deck: Every browser you use today runs on one of three engines. Ladybird built a fourth, from the ground up, and you no longer have to compile it yourself: there's a Mac download and Linux packages, with automatic updates.

title: The Morning Commit · Monday, November 23, 2026
lead: NTSCRT: turn any video into a 1995 CD-ROM clip, a worn VHS tape or a glowing CRT, with a free open-source app
deck: Finn McKenty's video-distortion app went viral with a new “Windows 95 CD-ROM” mode built on the actual old codec. It's MIT-licensed, has a command line and an MCP server, and a new release dropped overnight.

title: The Morning Commit · Sunday, November 22, 2026
lead: Drive a yellow cab through a sunset Manhattan, in your browser: mrdoob's Slop New York
deck: Ricardo Cabello (mrdoob), who created three.js, keeps adding features to Slop New York: a WebGPU city you can drive, fly a camera through, and teleport around, from the Empire State Building to Manhattanhenge.

title: The Morning Commit · Saturday, November 21, 2026
lead: A 26B open model that runs on a 16 GB laptop is the new local-AI favourite: Inkling 2 Mini
deck: Thinking Machines, the lab started by ex-OpenAI CTO Mira Murati, released Inkling 2 Mini with open weights. It re-runs part of itself three times per token to “think” without writing more, and people are already running it on MacBooks and gaming PCs.

title: The Morning Commit · Friday, November 20, 2026
lead: Someone put a tiny ChatGPT-style AI on a real Super Nintendo, and you can chat with it in your browser
deck: Tech journalist Benj Edwards had AI agents build an unofficial “ChatGPT for SNES”: a 2.2-million-parameter model that runs on the Doom-era Super FX 2 chip and types its answers one word at a time. It's often wrong, and that's half the fun.

title: The Morning Commit · Thursday, November 19, 2026
lead: nginx2root: the web server behind a huge chunk of the internet had a no-login remote takeover bug
deck: Several research teams independently found memory bugs in NGINX's HTTP/2 code that let a stranger run code on the server. One works on a plain static-file setup. Patched releases came out yesterday.

title: The Morning Commit · Wednesday, November 18, 2026
lead: HUMAN.md: a designer's weird, funny scrolling manifesto became the website everyone argued about
deck: Produce-headed dinner guests, scroll-triggered animations and one big question: what is a designer for when AI can make the average website in seconds?

title: The Morning Commit · Tuesday, November 17, 2026
lead: Lastbook, the free offline “rebuild society” library, broke the internet's download counter
deck: A free desktop app that packs survival guides, maps, how-to videos and a local AI chatbot. Once it's downloaded, it all works with the internet off.
